 IND U19 vs NEP U19: Sood Rocks Nepal, Aaryavir Lights Up the Chase in Father Virender’s Style
 -Ishan Sood bagged player of the match award with a three-for. -Aaryavir Sehwag and Lakshya Raichandani forger an unbeaten partnership of 129 to lead India’s ten-wicket win. -India will next face Pakistan on November 8. By Vaibhav Tripathi November 6, 2026 Updated: November 7, 2026 No Comments 3 Mins Read

 Riding on contrasting half-centuries from Aaryavir Sehwag and Lakshya Raichandani, coupled with an all-round bowling effort led by Ishan Sood, India secured an emphatic 10-wicket win over Nepal in their season opener of the U19 Men’s Asia Cup at the Al Amerat Cricket Ground. 
 There are two turfs at the Al Amerat Cricket Ground. India’s game was played on Turf 1, on the same wicket on which Afghanistan and Bangladesh had played the previous day. In that game, pacers from both teams exploited the conditions. Having followed the game closely, India must have gained a fair idea of the nature of the wicket.
 However, as they were playing the first game on this particular surface, the Colts in Blue decided to bowl first after winning the toss to assess the conditions.
 “Yeah, it was a good toss to win. There was some movement early on and we exploited it really well,” Raichandani said during the post-match presentation.
 As the captain had pointed out, there was movement on offer, and Sood utilised it to great effect. The tall pacer swung the ball both ways and did the damage with the new ball, taking all three wickets in his first spell. He bowled five overs in his opening spell. His match-defining figures of 3/18 in 10 overs included four maidens. With the old ball, he bowled quick, sharp bouncers while also mixing things up with the occasional slower delivery.
 The Indian spinners also had a great day, sharing six wickets among themselves. Arjun Rajput, Yashveer Goud and Manal Chauhan were among the wickets. Raichandani used a total of seven bowling options, including part-time options such as Yashbardhan Chauhan.
 India completed the run chase in a flash, reaching the target of 129 in 19.1 overs.
 Before the Nepal bowlers could settle into their rhythm, Aaryavir, much like his father Virender, took the attack to the bowlers right from the start in his innings of 70. There were flashes of senior Sehwag in Aaryavir, particularly in the way he played through the off side. The dynamic batter smashed seven fours and four sixes and finished the innings with a strike rate of 134.62. Junior Sehwag offered a glimpse of what the world can expect from him in the upcoming games.
 Raichandani watched Sehwag’s sparkling innings from the other end while playing a solid knock of 53 himself. Assurance and fine stroke play were on display from the Indian captain.
 Nepal fielded well, but their bowlers did not have enough runs to defend, as their batters had faltered.
 Next up, India will face arch-rivals Pakistan in a repeat of last year’s final on November 8.
